## The one-liner

> We integrated past Willamette application data and National Student Clearinghouse Data into one cohesive dataset so that
> the Willamette University Admissions and Enrollment Management teams can better allocate time and resources.

**Role:** I worked with data wrangling, modeling, and visualizations.
**Team:** [Seira Ramchandani](https://github.com/Seira-Ram/Seira-Ram.github.io)
**Repo:** [Public Repository](https://github.com/Data-Science-Capstone-Project-2026/Public_Repository/tree/main)

## The question

Willamette University spends a large amount of time and resources on recruitment and increasing enrollment. However, many students choose to enroll at another school. By understanding which type of school a student might enroll in, whether that be a large public school or another Northwest 5 school, the recruitment strategies can be tailored and potentially be more effective. 

## The data

The first set of data - Willamette Application Data from Slate - contained 9404 applications from 2023-2025. The second set of data - National Student Clearinghouse Data - was three separate csvs with information from 2023, 2024, and 2025. Both sets were joined on each applicant. For this data, privacy was extremely important. Both team members signed confidentiality agreements and the data was only accessible using a private key that only the team members had. 


## The approach

Firstly, we examined the data using Exploratory Data Analysis to see initial trends and identify which features would be worth keeping. We then moved into modeling, initially trying multinomial logistic regression, a support vector machine, and XGBoost. The support vector machine was not kept due to its lower precision scores. XGBoost also allowed for identifying the most important features, which was very helpful for the overall analysis.
